messages:
incident-bot: AUTOMATED PAGE: Synthetic canary failures detected in eu-west-1 (canary-group: inference-heartbeat). 12 consecutive failures across 3 probes. PagerDuty incident: PD-89234. Error: connection reset by peer.

pagerduty: PD-89234 triggered (severity: P2) — unacknowledged for 30s. Escalation policy: infra-canaries -> oncall-sre. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-89234

maria: saw the PD page, jumping in. seeing a cluster of 502/ECONNRESET in the probe logs.

ajay: +1, dashboard shows spike around 02:11 UTC. Throughput looks normal but canary latency for eu-west-1 is +800ms.

oncall-sre: acked PD-89234. taking initial triage. any customer reports?

maria: no inbound tickets in zendesk yet, but a few telemetry spikes from a small subset of hosts.

sam: sharing probe curl from control plane: `curl -v https://canary-eu1.redwood-infra/ping`

lindsay: output from `curl -v` shows `* Connection reset by peer` after SSL handshake.

ajay: running quick k8s check on canaries:
```
kubectl -n canary get pods -l app=canary-eu1 -o wide
# pods show Ready 2/2 except canary-3 restarting
kubectl logs canary-3 -c prober --tail=200
# repeated "read: connection reset by peer" in logs
```

maria: looks like one pod is flapping and causing probe fanout to fail. could be a local network issue or segfault.

oncall-sre: current plan: 1) cordon & drain canary-3; 2) temporarily increase probe timeouts to avoid noisy pages; 3) if failures persist, failover region routing for canary evaluations.

sam: cordon/drain commands ready: `kubectl cordon canary-3 && kubectl drain canary-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

lindsay: implemented probe timeout bump: updated prober config `timeout_ms: 1500 -> 3000` in configmap and applied. will watch for noise.

oncall-sre: cordoned canary-3 and drained successfully. new pod scheduled (canary-7).

incident-bot: CONFIG UPDATE: prober timeout updated in eu-west-1 (applied by lindsay).

pagerduty: PD-89234 acknowledged by oncall-sre (oncall-sre) at 2026-03-15T02:15:08Z.

maria: after draining, canary failures dropped to 0 for the last 3 checks. looks stable.

ajay: quick risk note: increasing timeouts may mask transient backend issues for a short window. recommend reverting after root cause.

oncall-sre: agree. root cause suspects: unstable instance network NIC on canary-3 host. I've opened a host investigation with infra to check node-level metrics and NIC errors.

lindsay: grabbed node logs and saw repeated `kernel: rmmod: ...` and `eth0: link reset` events around the same timeframe. attaching snippet to the incident later.

sam: rollback plan: restore original timeout and redeploy prober config once host verified or pod replaced.

maria: customer impact: none reported, but internal canary evals that trigger auto-rollouts may have been delayed. marking impact as "internal telemetry & gating only" for now.

oncall-sre: tagging PD incident PD-89234 with status: mitigated (temporary config), owner: infra-team for host remediation. Will hand off to infra for deep root cause and next steps.

pagerduty: PD-89234 status changed to "investigating" -> "resolved (mitigated)" by oncall-sre at 2026-03-15T02:22:45Z.

maria: adding followup action items: 1) infra to check NIC health and kernel logs on host-12; 2) add prober jitter to reduce synchronized retries; 3) add metric alert for pod restarts > 3 in 5m.

lindsay: noted. I’ll file a postmortem stub and link logs.

oncall-sre: handing off to infra oncall @ajay for follow-up. If infra confirms host-level fault, we will mark root cause and schedule a prevention ticket.

ajay: ack handoff. I’ll open an infra incident referencing PD-89234 and update once host analysis is done.

incident-bot: HANDOFF: oncall-sre -> infra-oncall (ajay).

maria: thanks everyone. closing Slack thread. I’ll keep the postmortem brief and link PD + logs. :white_check_mark:

sam: thanks — nice quick pivot. :thumbsup:
